input: Draft a complaint letter to the airline about delays

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific details of the delay (duration, number of flights affected, whether it caused a missed connection) determine what incidents and consequences to include in the letter.
Whether the letter is for one traveller or a group affects how it is framed and whether collective damages should be mentioned.
The airline name, flight number, route, and date ground the letter in verifiable facts and make it actionable.
Knowing whether the user has already contacted the airline or has a response deadline affects urgency and tone.
The desired tone — firm and legal, polite and diplomatic, or assertive — shapes the entire voice of the letter.
What the user wants as an outcome (refund, compensation voucher, miles, formal apology) determines what the letter demands and how strongly.
Whether the letter will be sent by email, physical mail, or via an online portal affects formatting, length, and whether attachments are referenced.

gold.taskTitle: Draft airline complaint letter about delays
gold.taskDescription: Write a formal complaint letter to an airline addressing a flight delay experience.

questions.title: How long was the delay, and did it cause any knock-on issues?
questions.description: Capture the delay duration and any cascading consequences such as missed connections, extra hotel stays, or lost bookings.

questions.title: Which airline, flight number, route, and travel date are involved?
questions.description: Identify the specific flight details needed to make the letter verifiable and credible.

questions.title: Who is the letter being written for — just you, or a group?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a solo complaint or on behalf of multiple passengers, which affects the framing and claimed damages.

questions.title: What outcome are you hoping to receive from the airline?
questions.description: Clarify the desired resolution — refund, compensation, flight voucher, miles, or a formal apology — so the letter can make a clear demand.

questions.title: What tone should the letter strike — polite, firm, or legally assertive?
questions.description: Establish the voice and register of the letter to match the user's preferred style and relationship with the airline.

questions.title: Have you already contacted the airline, or is this the first attempt?
questions.description: Knowing if prior contact was made (and what the airline's response was) affects whether this is an initial complaint or an escalation.

questions.title: Will this letter be sent by email, post, or an online complaints portal?
questions.description: The delivery method determines formatting choices, appropriate length, and whether supporting documents should be referenced as attachments.
